outcomes: A user gets the exact version every version line is at, derived from the line's git tags and the conventional commits that touch it, and releases a line with one command that writes its changelog, its release commit, and its tag
Two builds of one line never publish under one version: an untagged commit carries the ordered suffix above the line's last tag
A release is reviewable before it happens: version tag prints the proposed tag and its changelog and writes nothing without --yes
nonGoals: Declaring a version in the workspace, a scope, or a project document
Deriving a publication channel from the checked-out branch
Editing a version in place: version set and version bump no longer exist

requirements.text: A commit tagged with its line's pattern has the tag's version; a dirty tree is refused for publish; several tags on HEAD need --scope.
An untagged commit takes the line's last tag advanced by the conventional commits that touch the line, at least a patch, plus the ordered suffix; before 1.0 breaking and feat are minor.
A shallow clone or a checkout without tags is refused for version and publish; a full clone without a tag on the line yields 0.0.0.
version tag regenerates the line's changelog, creates the release commit, then the annotated tag on it.
